Het betreft een fulltime functie van 40 uur per week, waarin jij bijdraagt aan een betrouwbaar energienet. Bij Alliander krijg je volop de kans om door te groeien tot zelfstandig gasmonteur. Of je nu al ervaring hebt of nog aan het begin van je technische carrière staat. De energietransitie is onmogelijk zonder jou als aankomend gasmonteur Bij Liander werk je niet alleen aan de toekomst van het gasnet, maar ook aan je eigen ontwikkeling. Je volgt de mbo-3-opleiding tot gasmonteur. Eén dag per week ga je naar school, waar je reguliere vakken zoals Nederlands en Engels volgt, evenals gastechniek. Daarnaast werk je aan opdrachten en maak je verslagen hierover. De rest van de week leer je het vak samen met een ervaren monteur en doe je stap voor stap praktijkervaring op. Zo help je uiteindelijk mee met het oplossen van storingen en zorg je ervoor dat klanten weer kunnen rekenen op een veilig en betrouwbaar energienet. De praktijklessen vinden plaats op onze opleidingslocaties: in Heerhugowaard voor het westen van het land en in Zwolle voor het oosten en noorden. Vanaf dag één krijg je een Liander-bus tot je beschikking, zodat je goed voorbereid bent op weg kunt. Samen bouwen we aan het energienet van de toekomst – voor iedereen, met iedereen. En als aankomend gasmonteur draag jij daar elke dag aan bij. Zo ben jij onder andere bezig met: onderhouden en vervangen van aansluitleidingen, lage- en hogedruknetten en stations. aanleggen en inrichten van nieuwe installaties in distributienetten. oplossen van storingen bij de klant op een veilige en snelle manier. storingsdiensten draaien in de avonden en weekenden. Samen met jou maken we de energietransitie mogelijk, voor en mét onze klanten. En jij gaat dat doen bij ons bedrijfsonderdeel Liander. Hier ben jij medeverantwoordelijk voor het beheer en onderhoud van energienetten zoals elektriciteit en gas. Zo leveren wij energie aan huishoudens, bedrijven en andere klanten. Dat merk je door het begrip voor en interesse in elkaar. Jullie staan altijd voor elkaar klaar. En er is altijd ruimte voor een lolletje. Van de ene plek naar de andere rijden kan alleen als jij genoeg energie hebt. En de juiste werkomgeving geeft jou dat. De afdeling Onderhoud en storingen bestaat uit gezellige en behulpzame collega’s. Je leert dan ook veel van je leermeesters en van je andere collega-monteurs. Ook als iemand uitloopt met het werk staan we voor elkaar klaar. review_candidates.description: Global Schools Forum Director of Programmes Candidate Pack October 2026 About Global Schools Forum Global Schools Forum (GSF) connects and strengthens a global community of over 200 non-state education organisations across 70+ countries. Since 2017, we have become a leading accelerator for locally-led education innovation in Africa, Asia, and Latin America, supporting non-state education organisations to innovate, deepen impact, and achieve scale. We work as a global learning community, innovation accelerator, and partnership builder. We connect local leadership, share knowledge and insights, incubate and diffuse promising education solutions, and engage in policy-shaping dialogue to strengthen education systems. Our community collectively reaches 135 million children, and our Labs and Impact Accelerator programmes have supported innovations that now reach an additional one million children with better quality education and care. We are at an inflection point in our journey, having grown five-fold over the last five years. Our 2025–28 strategy marks an ambitious next chapter, with a renewed focus on community, knowledge, funding, and partnerships, and a deepening commitment to early years, foundational learning, secondary education, and leveraging technology. Our vision remains that all children realise their potential through safe access to quality education. GSF holds a role no other organisation in this sector plays: we are the connective tissue for organisations across low- and middle-income countries who are wrestling with the same hard problems, often without knowing who else is wrestling with them too. Our programmes turn that connective tissue into shared progress on some of education’s biggest challenges: Teaching children to read. Scaling access to high-quality early learning. Ensuring meaningful transitions into secondary education. Using artificial intelligence (AI) to drive learning. Join us at a moment of real momentum. We are positioned for additional significant growth, and the impact of this role will be felt in the quality and reach of our programmes portfolio, and in how well GSF’s largest team is set up to deliver it. We are a small, fully-remote global team with colleagues based in the UK and across Africa and Asia, reflecting the communities in which we work. We welcome applicants for this role from the UK, where we are headquartered, and the global south where we operate, with a preference for candidates within a time zone of GMT-2 to GMT+5:30. Role Purpose This is a rare opportunity to shape how GSF’s programmes are delivered, and how well our largest team is set up to deliver them. As Director of Programmes, you will sit on our Senior Management Team (SMT) and take strategic ownership of the portfolio that sits at the heart of GSF’s work. Programmes sit at the heart of this role. You will oversee our early learning, foundational learning, and secondary education portfolio, working closely with technical directors and associate directors so it delivers high impact for children and for the organisations we support. Alongside this, you will lead GSF’s largest team, putting in place the processes we need to allocate people well, learn across projects, and keep raising our operational bar. This is not a traditional programme management role. GSF’s programmes are tightly integrated with our community: the organisations we support are also our members, and our programmes are only valuable when they are fully informed by their needs, with informing collective action that can change practices in the classrooms and also influence governments and funders. You will be expected to hold that link deliberately, ensuring that we maintain trust with GSF’s community, that programme design is shaped by what we hear from our community, and that what we learn through delivery is shared back and drives meaningful change in practices in the classrooms and at the systems level. Portfolio Overview GSF’s programmes portfolio is organised across three areas: foundational learning, early childhood education and development, and a growing body of work in secondary education. Community strategy and engagement is owned across the senior management team and implemented by each member of the GSF team in a matrixed and collaborative way. Foundational learning Our foundational learning portfolio focuses on foundational literacy and numeracy (FLN): the systems and innovations needed to ensure all children can read, write, and count. This includes a growing body of work supporting organisations’ to strengthen their foundational learning programmes, with an increased focus on literacy. The portfolio also carries GSF’s dedicated focus on learning differences, innovative financing, and artificial intelligence (AI) in education, as lenses that inform how FLN programmes are designed and delivered. Across the portfolio, the work combines direct and high-impact support to education organisations with effective diffusion of practices and evidence-based advocacy with system stakeholders that can influence the broader sector. Early childhood education and development Our early childhood education and development (ECED) portfolio has a similar focus to the FLN portfolio includes a wide range of programmes for organisational support, evidence generation, and ecosystem influence. Examples include the Impact at Scale Labs and our Early Childhood in Emergencies Evidence Hub. The team is connecting practitioner insights with the broader evidence base, and bringing these messages into conversations with government, funders, and global policymakers. Secondary education Secondary education is a newer and growing body of work, building on our foundational learning expertise to support locally-led organisations as children move into secondary school, with several opportunities in the pipeline that would significantly scale the work. Community GSF’s community connects and supports our network of over 200 non-state education organisations across 70+ countries. Our community engagement strategy is shaped by the Senior Management Team (SMT), and its implementation is shared between two verticals, Programmes and External Affairs, each responsible for different parts of the strategy and drawing on time allocations from colleagues across the organisation. In this role, you will lead the Programmes vertical’s part of that implementation, working closely with External Affairs to drive growth, engagement, and the diffusion of promising practices. This role is more than excellent programme leadership, it is for someone who is purpose-driven, who brings genuine curiosity about how programmes translate into real change for children and collective action to move the sector, and about building the systems and the team that let GSF deliver at scale, not just overseeing delivery. How You Will Create Impact Programme judgement: you know where GSF’s programmatic effort will create the most impact for children, and you can prioritise a broad portfolio accordingly. Operational rigour: you turn learning from across projects into simple, practical systems that make delivery better, not just busier. People leadership: you build and support GSF’s largest team, giving people clarity, direction, and room to do their best work. Key Responsibilities Programme leadership and delivery (40%) Portfolio ownership: oversee the design, delivery, and quality of GSF’s programmes portfolio, spanning foundational learning, early childhood education and development, and a growing body of secondary education work. Technical collaboration: work with technical directors and associate directors across each portfolio area, including for Foundational Learning and Early Years, to ensure delivery is high-quality, evidence-based, and delivers real impact for children and for the organisations we support. Programme quality: establish and maintain clear standards for programme design, implementation, monitoring, and learning across all workstreams. Operational excellence (25%) Continuous improvement: identify opportunities to improve operational delivery across the portfolio, from planning and budgeting cycles through to reporting. Cross-project learning: facilitate learning across projects, connecting the dots across programmes so that good practice travels rather than staying siloed. Standard operating procedures: create and implement the standard operating procedures that keep delivery consistent, well-governed, and efficient. Team leadership (20%) Team management: manage GSF’s largest team, giving people clarity, direction, and room to do their best work. Resourcing: put in place, and own, the processes for allocating team members across projects, so the right expertise lands on the right work at the right time. Cross-functional deployment: work with functional leads across labs design, operations, technology, and evidence to make sure specialist expertise is well-deployed across the portfolio. Organisational leadership (15%) External representation: represent GSF in key external fora, linking practitioner insights, academic evidence and key system-level policies nationally and globally. Community strategy: lead the Programmes vertical’s part in implementing GSF’s community engagement strategy, as shaped by the SMT, working closely with External Affairs and drawing on time allocations from colleagues across the organisation, so that trust earned through our community work translates into shared momentum behind education’s biggest challenges. Diffusion and replication: champion two-way diffusion as standard practice, making sure community insight shapes how programmes are designed, and that what we learn through delivery reaches members and the sector in accessible, useful form. Senior management: participate in the SMT, contributing to organisational strategy and decision-making beyond the programmes portfolio. Person Specification We’re looking for someone who combines strong programme leadership with operational rigour: someone who brings energy, warmth, and strategic judgement to everything they do. Essential Significant senior experience leading education programmes at scale, with deep understanding of education program implementation in low- and middle- income countries and of the challenges and opportunities facing locally-led education organisations. Sound understanding and passion for building trust with a community of partner organisations to inform programmes and ensure that promising practices spread and get adopted elsewhere. Ability to engage with practitioners, as well as governments and funders to create collective movements that change practices in the sector. Strong commitment to locally-led approaches and to genuine partnership with the organisations GSF supports, listening carefully, responding to need, and avoiding the imposition of external agendas. A track record of leading complex, multi-workstream programme portfolios, managing multiple teams, funders, and delivery contexts simultaneously with rigour and care. A strong track record of managing large, distributed teams, including setting up the systems needed to allocate people well across multiple projects. Experience working closely with technical experts, such as technical directors or advisors, to translate technical excellence into high-quality delivery. A track record of improving operational delivery: spotting inefficiencies, building standard operating procedures, and embedding learning across projects. Strong strategic judgement, able to prioritise across a broad and varied portfolio. Experience working at, or preparing materials for, senior leadership or board level. A genuine commitment to GSF’s mission and values. Desirable Direct experience of programme implementation in foundational literacy and numeracy or early childhood education and development programming in low-resource or emergency-affected contexts. Experience in a membership or network organisation. Experience of AI in education, either in programme design and delivery or in understanding how AI tools can strengthen organisational effectiveness Terms and Conditions Location GSF is a fully remote organisation.
